vulnerability_analysis: The HuskyInu contract has a centralized blacklist mechanism controlled by the owner via the addBlacklist() function. The _transfer function checks require(!blacklist[sender] && !blacklist[recipient], 'BLACKLISTED'), which means any address added to the blacklist cannot send or receive tokens. This is a classic owner privilege abuse vulnerability where the owner can arbitrarily block any user from transacting with the token.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.startPrank() 2. Call addBlacklist(victim_address, true) to blacklist a victim 3. Verify the blacklist state is set to true for the victim address
step_by_step_plan: 1. Define IHuskyInu interface with addBlacklist and blacklist functions 2. In setUp(), create contract instance and identify owner 3. In testExploit(), use vm.startPrank(owner) to impersonate owner 4. Call addBlacklist(victim, true) 5. Assert blacklist[victim] == true
